back: The smallest particle of an element. It is made of protons, neutrons and electrons.
A substance made of only one type of atom. It can't be broken down into anything simpler by a chemical reaction.
Positive (+) charge, in the nucleus.
No charge (neutral), in the nucleus.
Negative (−) charge, moving around the nucleus. Electrons are much lighter than protons and neutrons.

front: What does the **atomic number** tell you?
back: The number of protons in each atom of the element. Every element has its own atomic number.

front: Why is an atom neutral overall?
back: It has the same number of electrons (−) as protons (+), so the charges cancel out.

front: What is a **group** in the periodic table?
back: A vertical column. Elements in the same group have similar chemical properties.

front: What is a **period** in the periodic table?
back: A horizontal row.

front: Where are the metals and non-metals in the periodic table?
back: Metals are on the left and in the centre. Non-metals are on the right, plus hydrogen at the top left.
Shiny, good conductors of heat and electricity, malleable and ductile, and mostly solids with high melting points.
Dull and brittle when solid, poor conductors (insulators), and many are gases at room temperature.
Soft metals that react quickly with water to make hydrogen and an alkaline solution. They get more reactive down the group.
Reactive metals, but less reactive than Group 1, e.g. magnesium burns with a bright white flame. They get more reactive down the group.
Very reactive non-metals that react with metals to make salts. They get less reactive and darker in colour down the group.
Colourless, very unreactive gases, e.g. helium (balloons), neon (signs) and argon (light bulbs).
He arranged the elements into a table by atomic mass and properties, left gaps for undiscovered elements and predicted their properties.

front: How is the modern periodic table ordered?
back: By atomic number (the number of protons).
The first letter is a capital; a second letter is lower case. Co is cobalt, but CO is carbon monoxide.
